full_judgment: 12. Mr Md Nurul Amin the learned Advocate for the plaintiffs-opposite parties opposes the Rule and submits that the trial Court without considering and discussing the evidence on record dismissed the suit and the appellate Court below upon proper appreciation and discussing the evidence on record allowed the appeal and reversing the decision of the trial Court. The trial Court wrongly held that the suit is barred by law of limitation but the learned appellate Court below with consideration of the materials evidence on record correctly held that the suit was filed within time, since the cause of action arisen on 20-4-2007 when the defendant No. 1 claimed the suit land on the basis of the illegal deed No. 1136 dated 19-7-1984 and the plaintiffs filed the instant suit on 16-5-2007. Even though the cause of action is counted from the dated 26-11-1996 when the defendant No. 1 transferred the suit land to the defendant Nos. 2-3, then it is clear that the suit was filed within 12 years but the learned trial Court illegally held that the suit is barred by law of limitation which was properly reversed by the appellate Court below. The learned trial Court illegally held that the suit is not maintainable for defect of parties since all the co-sharers of SA Khatian were not made party. The learned appellate Court below with proper consideration of fact reversed the issue on the ground that since the cases of both the parties that the suit land was belonged to Azgor Ali and the suit was for declaration of title, so all the co-sharers are not the necessary party of this suit and further held that admitted fact need not be proved under section 58 of the Evidence Act. The trial Court without considering the certified copy of the deed submitted by the plaintiffs, dismissed, the suit which is erred in law. If the certified copy of the deed is filed without calling for the original copy and without any objection the question of inadmissibility of this deed cannot be raised at a subsequent point of time. In the instant case the defendants did not raise any objection about the certified copy of the deed and the trial Court acted wrongly in not considering the deed and on the basis of this ground dismissed the suit. In this regard the learned Advocate has referred to the case of Joynal Abedin vs Mafizur Rahman, reported in 44 DLR (AD) 162. The plaintiffs filed the suit for declaration that the deed No. 1136 dated 19-7-1984 is forged, illegal and void, but the learned trial Court without discussing about the deed dated 19-7-1984, only discussed the deed No. 250 dated 12-2-1984 executed by Azgor Ali in favour of the plaintiff No. 1 held that the plaintiff No. 1 was not owner of the suit land. It is admitted by the defendant No.1 that the plaintiff owned the land from his father and as a result the defendant No.1 took a deed No. 1136 dated 19-7-1984 executed by the plaintiff side in favour of the defendant No. 1. If the defendant No. 1 willingly takes a deed from the plaintiff side, how the learned trial Court denied the ownership of the plaintiff, so it is clear that the trial Court erred in law in dismissing the suit and the appellate Court below with proper appreciation reversed the judgment of the trial Court. The trial Court without discussing the important issue regarding the burden of proof illegally dismissed the suit and the appellate Court below properly discussed the issue and held that when a deed is challenged as forged and fabricated documents, the onus of prove lies upon the defendants to prove whether the same is valid and genuine documents. Normally the initial burden of proving the execution of a document when it is denied must rest upon the person alleging its execution according to section 101 of the Evidence Act. In the present case, it is the case of the plaintiff side that the plaintiff side did not execute any sale deed dated 19-7-1984 in favour of the defendant No.1 and it was forged and fabricated document. On the other hand, it is the case of the defendants that the said sale deed is valid and genuine document. The sale deed itself is in possession of the defendant and in such a situation the defendants are in a dominating position to prove the documents affirmatively. In this situation the appellate Court below rightly held that the burden of prove lies upon the defendants to prove the document is valid and genuine. In this regard the learned Advocate referred the decisions delivered in the case of Aim Miah vs Gauranga Chandra Sharma, reported in 1 ADC 462 and Rishi vs Gurbaksh Singh, Supreme Court of India. The trial Court without discussing the issue, whether the suit is maintainable in its present form, just held that the suit is not maintainable in its present form which is barred in law and violated the mandatory provision of law under Order 20 rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The instant suit was filed for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and for further declaration that the sale deed No. 1136 dated 19-7-1984 is illegal, forged, collusive, null and void and nothing but a mere paper transaction and for cancellation of the said deed. The suit was filed under section 39 of the Specific Relief Act and ails the requirement of filing the suit was fulfilled by the plaintiffs and, as such, the suit is maintainable in its present form and the appellate Court below properly discussed the issue and rightly decreed the suit. PW 1 stated in his deposition dated 8-2-2009 that he wants possession. The learned Advocate for the defendants-petitioners claimed that since the plaintiff side is not in possession over the suit land, so the suit is not maintainable without praying for recover of khas possession. On 16-5-2005 the plaintiffs filed the Title Suit and prayed for recovery of khass possession if they were dispossessed during pendency of the suit by the defendants. In the instant suit the plaintiffs were dispossessed by the defendants after filing the Title Suit and, as such, the suit is maintainable, since he already prayed for recovery of khass possession in the plaint. It is a settled principle of law that the findings of fact, whether concurrent or not, arrived at by the appellate Court below which is the final Court of fact, is binding on the High Court Division' as revisional Court except in certain well-defined exceptional circumstances, such as non-consideration or misreading of the material evidence affecting the merit of the case. In the instant case, from the judgment of the appellate Court below it is found that in arriving at its findings the said Court carefully considered all the materials fact and circumstances of the case and evidence on record and consequently these findings of facts are immune from attack in revision. Since the learned Advocate for the defendants-petitioners did not point out any misreading, non-reading and non-consideration of material evidence on records, so in revisional jurisdiction, there is no scope for interfere in the judgment and decree of the appellate Court below and, as such, there is no merit in the Rule and the Rule is liable to be discharged. In this regard the learned Advocate has referred to the case of Hazari Bala Sana vs Niron alias Niranjan Mandal, reported in 1997 BLD (AD) 294.
